title: Air Ambulance Crew Repels to the Rescue, Package
description: Package about Basra's 2515 Air Ambulance crew staying prepared for air medical evacuations by conducting evacuation training by rappelling from a tower. Includes soundbites from Air Force Master Sgt. Jules Roy - 2515 air ambulance team leader from West Hampton Beach, N.Y. and Navy Petty Officer 2nd Class Dwayne Thompson - air crew survival crewman from Brooklyn, N.Y. Produced by Spc. Jenna Lindauer.
keywords: repelling, Jenna Lindauer, rappelling, Air Ambulance, Jules Roy, West Hampton Beach, Dwayne Thompson, training, medical, tower, evacuation, Brooklyn, NY

transcript.text: Heights aren't for everyone, but for Bosras 2515 air ambulance crew,
scaling a 150 foot tower was just another day of training.
The crew does air medical evacuations. To stay prepared for any situation,
they practice high angle litter evacuations from Bosra Airport's air traffic control tower.
One of our skill sets as pararescament is to
evacuate members of the military. Some sort of high angle terrain,
whether it be a kind of mountainous terrain or there would be something in an industrial environment.
Any evacuation scenario centers on teamwork, good communication and technical skills.
One of the patients talked about his confidence in his team.
When I went down the litter shifted a little bit, so I was at an angle.
So when I was up there I thought I was gonna fall at first, but again I trust these guys.
I know what they're gonna do. The air ambulance crew is the only one of its kind in Iraq.
The patients on the ground slack.
They'll continue conducting periodic training on the tower to keep their skill sharp.
